title: Robert Pattinson to apply for 90,000 more jobs? UK government trolls James Bond actor
summary:
Westminster joins wave of ‘job-stealing’ memes after the actor’s late success edging out the other contenders to be the new 007

Everybody is trying to get a piece of the Bond action: even…

blocks.text: Everybody is trying to get a piece of the Bond action: even the UK government.

In a post on its official Instagram account, the UK government promoted its youth jobs guarantee scheme, first announced in August, with a picture of Robert Pattinson as Bond with the joke caption: “Robert Pattinson to apply for all 90,000 jobs created for young people through Youth Employment Scheme.”

The post, which was also shared by the Department for Work and Pensions, is a reference to the flood of memes that has followed Pattinson’s casting as Bond, after the actor’s seemingly late intervention in the process. “Job stealing” posts have multiplied, with gags such as “AI won’t take my job. Robert Pattinson will” receiving millions of likes. Ralph Fiennes, whose intial response to the Bond casting news was to say “I’m still in love with Daniel Craig”, jokingly replied to a question as to who might play Voldemort in the new Harry Potter TV series by saying, “Maybe they’ll offer it to Robert Pattinson”.

Clips have also resurfaced of Pattinson in a 2025 Vanity Fair “lie detector” interview alongside Jennifer Lawrence in which he, not entirely seriously, said in response to a question as to whether he would make another Twilight movie: “I like taking jobs from younger actors … I want to play 17 again.”

The memes also demonstrate affectionate concern for the other actors in contention for the role, particularly Nicholas Hoult who, like Pattinson, was apparently a last-minute addition to the shortlist, with social media users commiserating with Hoult for losing out on Bond, as well as other high profile roles such as Superman.
The UK government’s move to troll Pattinson appears to have paid off, with over 117,000 likes and more than 1,400 comments on its post at the time of writing.
